schema: Anthropic long-running-agent feature list (category / description / steps / passes), extended with id / blockedBy / refs. See https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents
instructions: Edit ONLY the `passes` field of a feature, and flip it to true ONLY after carefully testing every step. Never delete, weaken, or merge a feature to make it pass. Work the highest-priority feature whose blockedBy are all passing. UI-only: do not modify strata-daemon (ADR-0003).

features.title: Empty visor
features.description: The extension installs, enables, and supervises the Strata daemon; Ctrl+Alt+C makes a full-width, fixed-height empty visor appear instantly at the configured edge and toggle away.
steps: gnome-extensions enable activates the extension with no errors in the journal
Ctrl+Alt+C instantly shows a full-width band (~360px) at the bottom edge and toggles it away on the same key; no slide animation
Escape and focus-loss dismiss the visor
The daemon is spawned if absent, supervised with exponential-backoff restart, and NOT double-spawned when a systemd instance already owns dev.edu4rdshl.Strata

features.title: Shelf from history
features.description: The visor renders clipboard history as a horizontal shelf of fixed-width Text cards, newest first, paginated from the daemon and loading more as you scroll toward the end.
steps: On open, the first page (page-size, default 50) loads via GetHistory(0, pageSize) and renders as ~300x280 cards, ~6 visible on 1080p
Scrolling within ~200px of the end fetches the next page; the full table never sits in JS memory
Rows are inserted in idle_add batches (~20) so a page never freezes a frame
Card text uses St.Label only (no set_markup)

features.title: Image thumbnails
features.description: Image entries show a thumbnail on their card, fetched on demand only for visible cards and cached to disk.
steps: Image cards render a placeholder first, then load the ~200px PNG via GetThumbnail(id) for visible cards only
Thumbnails are cached at ~/.cache/strata/thumbnails/<id>.png and reused (session Map + disk)
Scrolling past off-screen image cards issues no D-Bus traffic for those rows
On ItemDeleted, the cached thumbnail file is unlinked

features.title: Search (FTS5 prefix)
features.description: Typing in the header search box filters the shelf via the daemon's FTS5 prefix search. Fuzzy search is deferred to v2 (ADR-0003).
steps: Search box is focused on open (search-first); typing filters results
Queries call SearchHistory(query, max-history) with a 150ms debounce and an epoch guard that drops stale responses
Empty query restores the recent-history browse view
Results render through the same paged/idle_add mechanism as browse mode

features.title: Select & copy-and-dismiss
features.description: Choosing a card copies that entry to the system clipboard and dismisses the visor. No auto-paste (ADR-0005).
steps: Enter copies the focused card (or the top result if focus is still in search) and closes the visor
Alt+1...9 copies the Nth visible card and closes
Paste-back fetches GetItemContent(id): text via St.Clipboard.set_text, binary via Meta.SelectionSourceMemory + set_owner
No synthetic paste is ever sent to another app
move-activated-to-top is honored when the setting is on

features.title: Peek (Space)
features.description: Space enlarges the focused card into a Peek: full text (syntax-highlighted for code) or a full-resolution image.
steps: Space on a text/code card shows the full content large; code is syntax-highlighted (highlight.js) ONLY here, never on the shelf
Space on an image card shows the full-resolution image, decoded on demand via GetItemContent (one image, on keypress)
Space again or Escape dismisses the Peek back to the shelf
Highlighting/decoding happens only for the single Peeked entry

features.title: Card renderers (URL, color, file)
features.description: Non-plain-text entries get type-specific cards matching Strata's current behavior: URL, hex color, file(s). Cheap client-side regex; no code detection on the shelf (ADR-0007).
steps: Entries matching a URL render link-styled with the hostname as a subtitle
Entries matching #rgb / #rrggbb render a hex color swatch
uri-list / copied-files entries render filename(s) with an icon
Classification is cheap regex on the client; everything else stays a Text card

features.title: Settings (in-UI gear + layout keys)
features.description: A gear in the visor header opens the extension prefs directly, and the new layout keys are wired into the gschema and the visor.
steps: A gear button opens the prefs window via openPreferences() without going through the GNOME Extensions app (req #5)
Prefs expose visor-edge (top/bottom, default bottom), visor-height, card-width, plus the reused Strata keys (theme, max-history, size caps, keyboard-shortcut, excluded-apps)
Changing visor-edge/height/card-width updates the visor live or on next open
theme auto/light/dark applies via the class-toggle approach

features.title: Live updates (signals)
features.description: The shelf stays in sync with the daemon via its D-Bus signals.
steps: ItemAdded prepends a new card (debounced to coalesce bursts); entries from excluded-apps are dropped
ItemDeleted removes the card and unlinks its cached thumbnail
HistoryCleared empties the shelf and wipes the thumbnail cache directory

features.title: Capture clipboard from other apps
features.description: Copies made in other apps reach Strata. On GNOME the daemon's data-control monitor cannot bind (Mutter exposes neither ext- nor wlr-data-control, see strata-daemon/src/clipboard/monitor.rs), so the extension is the capture agent: it watches the Meta selection and forwards each new payload to the daemon via SubmitItem. Missed in v1 (only daemon supervision, proxy, focus tracking, and signals were lifted from strata@edu4rdshl.dev) so history only grew while the original extension was also enabled. Port _connectClipboardMonitor / _readClipboard / _pickMime + SubmitItem from strata@edu4rdshl.dev/extension.js.
steps: Copying text/image/uri-list in another app stores it: a Meta selection owner-changed read picks the best MIME (allowlist mirroring the daemon pick_mime / the original extension) and calls SubmitItem(mime, ay) with the raw bytes, off the main thread (transfer_async into a MemoryOutputStream, no synchronous base64)

Rapid clipboard writes are debounced (~50ms) and only one transfer_async is in flight at a time; payloads over the size cap (max-text-mb / max-image-mb) and x-kde-passwordManagerHint secrets are skipped
Size caps are pushed to the daemon via SetConfig on enable and when the keys change, so the History prefs take effect

TEST FIRST: verify.sh case 010 stubs _proxy.SubmitItemRemote to record (mime, bytes); drives the nested session clipboard (St.Clipboard.set_text for text, a SelectionSourceMemory owner for an image); asserts SubmitItem fires once per copy with the right mime and decoded bytes, that an over-cap payload and a passwordManagerHint offer are dropped, and statically that owner-changed + transfer_async + SubmitItem exist in extension.js. RED before impl (no capture today), GREEN after; 002 + 009 re-verified
Manual live smoke: with only strata-ui enabled, copy text in another app and confirm a new card appears

features.title: Keyboard navigation across the shelf (Left/Right)
features.description: Left/Right move the selection across the horizontal shelf. Live bug: the search entry's ClutterText consumes the arrow keys for its text cursor, so navigation never reaches the shelf and focus stays stuck in search. Fix: intercept Left/Right in the captured-event (capture) phase, like Space/Peek already is. Right enters the shelf from the search box; Left steps back off the first card to the search box. Trade: arrows navigate cards instead of moving the search cursor, which is expected for a launcher (Home/End/Backspace still edit the query).
steps: With the visor open and focus in the search box, Right moves key focus to the first card and Right again to the next; the target is scrolled into view
Left walks back through the cards and, stepping off the first card, returns focus to the search box (moveFocus returns a boolean the capture handler uses to hand focus back)
Arrow handling lives in the captured-event phase so the search entry never swallows it; the dead bubble-phase Left/Right block is removed

TEST FIRST: verify.sh case 011 opens with browse cards, focuses the search clutter_text, sends a REAL Right keystroke (nested_key Right), asserts global.stage key focus is now the first card; Right -> second card; Left x2 -> back in the search box. RED before impl (today the keystroke stays in search), GREEN after; 004 + 005 + 006 re-verified

features.title: Paste-back writes the chosen entry (end-to-end)
features.description: Choosing a card must place THAT entry on the system clipboard. Live bug: it pasted the most-recent entry instead. The 005 test only asserted the internal _lastWrite field, not the real clipboard, so the regression passed headlessly. This slice adds an end-to-end clipboard read-back test and fixes the cause. Suspect: activate() fires _pasteBack un-awaited and dismisses immediately (onPick), whereas the known-good original (strata@edu4rdshl.dev panel.js _onItemActivated) awaits GetItemContent and writes the clipboard BEFORE closing. Confirm against the live journal before settling on the fix.
steps: After activating a non-top card, the system clipboard actually holds THAT card's content (read back via St.Clipboard.get_text in the nested session), not the top-of-history entry

The clipboard write is not lost when the visor dismisses: GetItemContent resolves and the clipboard is set even though the visor closes (write before dismiss, matching the original _onItemActivated ordering)

TEST FIRST: verify.sh case 012 puts real items in the daemon (SubmitItem) so they exist, opens browse, activates a known non-top card, then READS the real nested-session clipboard (St.Clipboard.get_default().get_text) and asserts it equals that card's content (end-to-end, not just _lastWrite). RED if the bug reproduces headlessly, GREEN after. Only if the headless clipboard already comes back CORRECT is the bug session-specific — then, and only then, capture the live journal. 005 re-verified
Fallback live smoke (only if headless cannot reproduce): click an older entry, paste into a text editor, confirm it matches; capture journalctl '[Strata UI]' lines

features.title: Gear opens the preferences window (live)
features.description: The header gear hides the visor then calls openPreferences(); live, the visor closes but no prefs window appears. The likely cause is prefs.js failing to construct under the running GNOME's libadwaita (008 only node --check-ed it, which cannot catch a runtime Adw API change/removal, e.g. Adw.MessageDialog in the shortcut dialog). This IS headless-testable: drive the real prefs path against the nested shell and assert prefs.js loads without error. Harden _onGearClicked so a prefs failure is logged with the [Strata UI] prefix instead of failing silently.
steps: Clicking the gear opens the Strata UI prefs window (General + Privacy pages) and does not merely dismiss the visor
Any Adw API incompatibility in prefs.js for the running GNOME (48/49/50) is fixed; prefs.js constructs cleanly
_onGearClicked wraps openPreferences in try/catch and logs failures; opening prefs does not depend on the visor's modal still being up

TEST FIRST: verify.sh case 013 invokes the REAL prefs path in the nested shell (org.gnome.Shell.Extensions.OpenExtensionPrefs on the private bus, the same call openPreferences() makes), then asserts there is NO prefs/Adw error in the shell log and screenshots the prefs window. Keep the 008 spy that the gear handler calls openPreferences(). RED if prefs.js throws under the running Adw, GREEN after the fix. Live journal only as a fallback if it loads clean headlessly yet still fails in the real session

features.title: Install docs: one Strata extension at a time
features.description: install.sh must tell the user to disable strata@edu4rdshl.dev and enable strata-ui@elijahlynn.net (Extensions app or the gnome-extensions CLI), and that Wayland needs a log out / back in before a brand-new extension can be enabled. Running both extensions makes them fight over daemon supervision, the Ctrl+Alt+C binding, and clipboard capture.
steps: install.sh prints, in order: log out/in on Wayland first, then disable strata@edu4rdshl.dev, then enable strata-ui@elijahlynn.net, then Ctrl+Alt+C to toggle
If strata@edu4rdshl.dev is currently enabled, install.sh warns about the conflict
TEST: verify.sh case 014 statically asserts install.sh references disabling strata@edu4rdshl.dev and enabling strata-ui@elijahlynn.net

features.title: Harness: run the full regression suite every slice
features.description: Regressions are currently caught only if the agent remembers to re-run neighbouring cases by hand (verify.sh runs a single id; coding-prompt.md only requires the current id). Make the full suite enforced. BUILD THIS FIRST (before 010-014) so every later slice is gated by it, even though its id is higher than theirs.
steps: verify.sh grows an 'all' mode: `bash test-harness/verify.sh all` runs the case for every feature id that has a case block, prints a per-id PASS/FAIL summary, and exits non-zero if ANY case fails
coding-prompt.md step 5 (and the Red step) require `verify.sh all` to be green before flipping passes / committing, not just the current id
AGENTS.md regression rule points at `verify.sh all`
TEST: `verify.sh all` on the current tree runs all built cases and the summary lists every id; temporarily breaking one case makes the run exit non-zero (then revert the break)

features.title: Test clipboard corpus (3 of each claimed type)
features.description: Every verify case rolls its own inline, almost-all-TEXT stub; there is no shared corpus and no case ever loads a REAL image — which is exactly why the image paste-back bug shipped (the binary path was never exercised). Build one reusable corpus of realistic clipboard items — 3 of EACH claimed type, with REAL bytes — plus a loader the cases share. 'Claimed types' are taken FROM THE SOURCE, not invented: the union of docs/reference/strata-daemon-dbus-contract.md ('Supported MIME'), strata@edu4rdshl.dev/extension.js _pickMime PREFERRED allowlist, and the cardTypes extension/ui/card.js classify() renders (image, file, link, color, text). The corpus covers plain text, html, rtf, markdown, file (text/uri-list + gnome-copied-files), raster images (REAL small PNG bytes plus jpeg/gif/bmp/webp), the link regex card (real URLs) and the color regex card (real #hex). The loader seeds the corpus into the throwaway daemon via SubmitItem (preferred — exercises capture + storage + thumbnailing, including the real binary image path) or stubs the shelf's _fetchPage seam with it.
steps: test-harness/corpus/ holds 3 realistic items of each claimed type with REAL bytes: real small PNGs (and jpeg/gif/bmp/webp), real text/uri-list and gnome-copied-files, real html/rtf/markdown/plain-text, 3 real URLs, 3 real #hex colors, described by manifest.json (file, mime, expected cardType)

test-harness/corpus/loader.js exposes a loader callable from verify cases: seedViaSubmit(baseDir, proxy, cb) pushes each item's raw bytes into the daemon via SubmitItem (images go through the binary ay path), and stubFetchPage(shelf, baseDir) builds ItemMeta[] from the corpus and overrides the shelf seam for daemon-free classification/render asserts

TEST FIRST: verify.sh case 016 loads the corpus and asserts each type classifies to the correct cardType and renders its type-specific body — image -> thumbnail container, file -> filename, link -> hostname subtitle, color -> swatch, text (incl. html/rtf/markdown) -> St.Label — and that real PNG bytes (\x89PNG magic) reach the daemon via SubmitItem. RED before the corpus/loader exists, GREEN after
TEETH: breaking a renderer or the loader turns case 016 RED; restoring it returns green

Image paste-back is NOT asserted here: pushing a REAL image through full paste-back exposes the known image-paste bug ('No compatible transfer format found'), which is a separate slice — case 016 asserts image RENDERING only and records the image-paste gap as a follow-up

features.title: Copy image also offers a file path (paste into text apps)
features.description: When an image is copied, Strata ALSO writes a text file:// path to a temp file holding the image, alongside the image bytes. A VTE/text terminal (GNOME Console, and Claude Code in it) cannot accept an image on paste from ANY clipboard source (confirmed: even GNOMEs native screenshot clipboard fails into KGX), so a file path is the only way to get an image into a text target. Image-accepting apps still take the bytes. Decided: always offer the path, not behind a setting. BLOCKED — same Mutter/GJS wall as 019, verified empirically on GNOME Shell 50.1 / Mutter 18 / GJS 1.88. The slice requires ONE clipboard owner advertising image/png AND text/uri-list AND text/plain at once (image app takes the bytes, terminal takes the path). On Mutter a GJS extension can only own the selection via (a) Meta.SelectionSourceMemory.new(mimetype, content) — single-mime by construction; or (b) St.Clipboard.set_text / set_content — also single text-family / single mimetype; both REPLACE the owner (verified: image-owner-then-text-owner leaves only text readable, get_mimetypes='', image read returns null — Mutter clobbers, never merges). The only API that could serve several mimes from one owner is a custom Meta.SelectionSource subclass, but GJS CANNOT register it: overriding vfunc_read_async fails at registerClass with 'VFunc read_async accepts another callback as a parameter. This is not supported', and the base read_async serves no bytes. The temp-file write is trivially doable UI-only, but with no multi-mime owner it cannot be offered ALONGSIDE the image bytes — serving only a uri-list/text path would DROP the image/png bytes that image-paste targets (Gmail/Warp, confirmed working in 019) negotiate for, regressing them; weakening the slice to a path-only owner is not allowed. The daemon's SetClipboard(id) (wl-clipboard-rs copy_multi, multi-format) is unavailable on Mutter (no ext-/wlr-data-control — same failure 019 documented) AND is single-mime for images in writer.rs, so even that would need a Rust change (ADR-0003). Real fix is daemon-side (a Mutter-native multi-format selection owner, or teach the write path) and is deferred to v2. Keep passes:false; ship no impl; add NO permanently-RED case 022) (it would break verify.sh all for the whole suite, slice 015). SUPERSEDED FOR THE REAL USE CASE (user-confirmed 2026-06-27): selecting an image in Strata puts the image bytes on the clipboard via the existing paste-back (Meta.SelectionSourceMemory), and Ctrl+V into Claude Code pastes the image successfully — so the motivating case (get a Strata image into Claude running in a terminal) ALREADY WORKS with no file-path. 022 stays passes:false and is DEPRIORITIZED/effectively wontfix for v1: the multi-mime wall still blocks offering a file:// path ALONGSIDE the bytes, and such a path is now only marginally useful for pure-text VTE paste targets that take text but not the Ctrl+V image path.
steps: Intended: on image paste-back, save the image to a temp file (e.g. ~/.cache/strata/paste/<id>.<ext>) and offer BOTH the image bytes AND its file:// path as text (text/uri-list + text/plain)
Intended: pasting an image into a text terminal yields the file path; into an image app yields the image bytes
Intended TEST: activate an image corpus item; read the clipboard as a text client and assert the file:// path; as an image client and assert the bytes; teeth-proven
Intended: clean up temp files (unlink on next copy / on disable)

RESULT (empirical, GNOME 50.1 / Mutter 18 / GJS 1.88): no UI-only multi-mime clipboard owner exists. Meta.SelectionSourceMemory is single-mime; St.Clipboard set_text/set_content are single text-family / single mimetype; both replace (clobber) the owner — verified by writing image then text and reading back: only the last owner survives, get_mimetypes returns just its own mime. A custom Meta.SelectionSource cannot be subclassed in GJS (vfunc_read_async 'accepts another callback as a parameter. This is not supported'). The daemon SetClipboard path is dead on Mutter (no data-control) and single-mime for images anyway. Cannot serve image bytes + file path together without a daemon change (ADR-0003). passes:false; no impl; no verify case.

features.title: Typing on a focused card routes to the search box (Up returns to search)
features.description: When a card has keyboard focus, any printable typing key (not Left/Right which navigate, not Space=Peek / Enter=copy / Delete=delete) should redirect to the search box and type there; and Up should move focus from a card back to the search box. Currently typing on a focused card is lost (St.Button takes no text input), so a user cannot refine the search after arrowing into the cards. DO NOT BUILD until directed.
steps: With a card focused, pressing a printable character focuses the search box and types it (route or re-inject the keystroke so the character is not lost)
With a card focused, Up moves focus back to the search box
Left/Right still navigate; Space/Enter/Delete card actions unchanged
TEST: focus a card, send a printable key, assert focus is in search and the char reached the query; send Up, assert focus in search; teeth-proven

features.title: Search box placeholder text contrast
features.description: Live bug (user-reported): the search box placeholder/hint text 'Search clipboard…' (shown while the entry is empty) renders near-WHITE and is hard to read against the visor band. St.Entry draws the hint as a StLabel.hint-text child whose colour, unstyled by us, fell back to the GNOME default theme rule `StEntry StLabel.hint-text { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.7) }` — near-white in BOTH our skins, so it nearly vanished on the pale light band and washed out on the dark one. Fix: give the hint a readable, well-contrasting colour per theme in extension/stylesheet.css, distinctly dimmer than typed text but easily legible, with selectors specificity-matched (.strata-search StLabel.hint-text plus the .strata-theme-* variants) so the default theme rule can't out-specify them.
steps: The empty-search placeholder uses a readable colour with good contrast on the band in BOTH themes (dark and light), distinctly dimmer than typed text but easily legible; it is no longer the near-white rgba(255,255,255,0.7) default

.strata-search StLabel.hint-text (and the per-theme .strata-theme-dark / .strata-theme-light variants) are matched in specificity so the GNOME default StEntry StLabel.hint-text rule can't out-specify them

TEST FIRST: verify.sh case 017 opens the visor in each skin and reads the hint label's COMPUTED foreground colour via St.Entry.get_hint_actor().get_theme_node().get_foreground_color(); it asserts the colour equals the intended readable value, is NOT the near-white rgb(255,255,255), and clears a WCAG contrast bar (>=4.5:1) against the band background. RED on the current CSS, GREEN after the fix
TEETH: setting the hint colour back to the old near-white turns case 017 RED (the light-band contrast collapses to ~1:1); restoring the readable colour returns green

features.title: Crisp card thumbnails (no blurry upscaling)
features.description: Image cards render very blurry / low-res. card.js applyThumbnail() sets the daemon's ~200px thumbnail as a background-image with `background-size: cover`, which upscales it to fill the ~300px card (worse on a HiDPI/scaled display) and crops it to the card's aspect. Fix is UI-only: render the thumbnail without blurry upscaling — `background-size: contain` keeps it crisp at its native size, preserves aspect (no crop), and letterboxes the remainder against the card's dark thumb background. This is the UI-only ceiling: a TRULY sharp HiDPI card needs the daemon to emit a larger thumbnail (a GetPreview(id, max_px) endpoint), which crosses ADR-0003 and is NOT done here.
steps: applyThumbnail() applies the fetched thumbnail with `background-size: contain` (crisp at native size, aspect-preserving, letterboxed), never `cover`
Image cards still show a placeholder first and swap in the thumbnail for visible cards only (003 behavior unchanged: container, on-demand fetch, disk cache, unlink-on-delete)

TEST FIRST: verify.sh case 018 stubs the fetch seams with image metas, opens, and asserts the applied _thumbContainer.style uses `background-size: contain` and does NOT use `cover`. TEETH: reverting applyThumbnail back to `cover` turns case 018 RED. 003 re-verified

HONEST NOTE: contain caps upscaling for crispness but cannot add resolution; truly-sharp HiDPI thumbnails require a larger daemon thumbnail (crosses ADR-0003 — daemon untouched). This slice is the UI-only ceiling.

features.title: Delete key removes the focused item
features.description: With a card highlighted (keyboard focus), pressing Delete removes THAT clipboard item from history. Live bug: Delete on a focused card does nothing. Fix: the visor's key handling, on Delete / KP_Delete when a card holds focus, calls a shelf method that deletes the focused card's item via the daemon's DeleteItem (DeleteItemAsync). The daemon emits ItemDeleted, which shelf.onItemDeleted already handles (drops the card + unlinks the cached thumbnail); focus then moves to the next card. Delete with focus in the search box must NOT delete (it edits the query text there).
steps: With the visor open and a card focused, Delete (or KP_Delete) calls DeleteItem(id) for that card's id; the daemon's ItemDeleted then removes the card and unlinks its cached thumbnail
After a delete, key focus moves to the next card (or the previous one if the deleted card was last), so repeated Delete walks the shelf
Delete while focus is still in the search box does NOT delete an item (Delete edits the search text); no DeleteItem is issued

TEST FIRST: verify.sh case 020 opens with browse cards, focuses a card, sends a REAL Delete keystroke (nested_key Delete), and asserts DeleteItem was called for that card's id (recording stub on the proxy) and the card is removed once ItemDeleted lands; asserts a real Delete with focus in the search box issues NO DeleteItem. RED before impl (Delete does nothing today), GREEN after. TEETH: removing the Delete handler turns it RED

features.title: Gear re-click refocuses an already-open prefs window
features.description: Live bug: when the Strata UI prefs window is ALREADY open but not focused (it sits behind another window), clicking the gear again appears to do nothing. Root cause is in GNOME Shell's own extensions D-Bus service (dbusServices/extensions/extensionsService.js, GNOME 50): OpenExtensionPrefs throws 'Already showing a prefs dialog' when this._prefsDialog already exists, so a second openPreferences() is rejected and the existing window is never raised or presented. The prefs window lives in a SEPARATE gjs process (org.gnome.Shell.Extensions), so the extension cannot present() it directly — but the Shell side CAN find that window among Mutter's windows (by the extension's display name / gtk-application-id) and Main.activateWindow() it (raise + focus + switch workspace). Fix _onGearClicked so a gear re-click RAISES the existing window: look up an open prefs window for this extension first and activate it; only call openPreferences() to open a fresh one when none exists. Keep the existing deferred-open (past the modal-grab teardown) and the '[Strata UI] gear clicked' log.
steps: Clicking the gear while a prefs window is already open (but unfocused/behind another window) raises and refocuses that EXISTING window instead of no-opping

_onGearClicked looks up an open prefs window for this extension (matched by the extension's display name / gtk-application-id among global.get_window_actors()) and, when found, calls Main.activateWindow() on it to raise+focus; when none is found it falls back to openPreferences() to open a fresh one

The existing deferred-open behaviour is preserved (the open/raise still runs one idle tick AFTER _hideVisor() pops the modal grab, so it does not depend on the grab still being up) and the '[Strata UI] gear clicked' log line is kept

TEST (headless, what is legitimately observable): verify.sh case 021 asserts statically that _onGearClicked has a present/raise path (Main.activateWindow + a window-lookup helper matching by name/gtk-application-id) and keeps the openPreferences fallback + the gear-clicked log; and at runtime stubs the window-lookup seam to inject a FAKE existing prefs window, spies Main.activateWindow, and asserts a gear click ACTIVATES that existing window (raise path taken) and does NOT open a second fresh prefs dialog — while a gear click with NO existing window calls openPreferences() exactly once (the open path). This proves the branch + the raise/activate call deterministically without the real cross-process window.

LIVE-SMOKE-GATED (cannot be headless-verified): the REAL prefs window lives in a separate gjs process (org.gnome.Shell.Extensions) and cannot be created or observed from the throwaway nested shell (the 013 agent proved this). The end-to-end refocus is therefore verified MANUALLY, not by a headless assertion: (1) Ctrl+Alt+C, click the gear to open Strata UI prefs; (2) click another window so the prefs window loses focus and is hidden behind it; (3) Ctrl+Alt+C, click the gear again; (4) confirm the SAME prefs window is raised to the front and refocused (no second window opens). passes:true is set on the strength of this manual verification plus the headless branch/raise-call coverage above — NOT on a faked headless green for the cross-process raise.

features.title: Image paste-back offers compatible formats
features.description: Live, reproducible: pasting an IMAGE copied from Strata works in apps that accept image/png (Gmail, Warp) but FAILS in KGX / GNOME Console with 'g-io-error-quark (15): No compatible transfer format found'. Cause: shelf.js _writeClipboard writes binary/image items through Meta.SelectionSourceMemory.new(mime, bytes), which advertises exactly ONE mime type. Text works because St.Clipboard.set_text publishes several text formats; images offer only one, so a consumer that negotiates for a different format (e.g. image/bmp) gets nothing. The intended UI-only fix was to route the binary/image paste-back path through the daemon's existing SetClipboard(id), which uses wl-clipboard-rs copy_multi to publish multiple formats — calling an existing daemon API, no Rust change (ADR-0003). BLOCKED — verified empirically NOT possible from this stack: (1) SetClipboard(id) on GNOME/Mutter returns 'org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: A required Wayland protocol (ext-data-control, or wlr-data-control version 1) is not supported by the compositor' and leaves the Mutter clipboard untouched (a pre-set sentinel survives), because wl-clipboard-rs needs the data-control protocol that Mutter exposes to neither monitor nor write (the daemon itself logs 'Wayland clipboard monitor unavailable, using GJS Meta.Selection path (expected on GNOME)'); (2) even if it could own the clipboard, strata-daemon/src/clipboard/writer.rs offers NON-text (image) blobs a single mime in its else-branch — so SetClipboard would NOT deliver multi-format for images without a Rust change anyway; (3) there is no UI-only multi-mime alternative on Mutter — GJS cannot subclass Meta.SelectionSource (vfunc_read_async 'accepts another callback as a parameter. This is not supported') and Meta.SelectionSourceMemory is single-mime by construction. The only real fix (teach the daemon's write path to offer multiple image formats AND/or a Mutter-native multi-format selection owner) crosses ADR-0003 (daemon change) and is deferred to v2. Keep passes:false; do not fake green; do not add a permanently-RED case 019) that would break verify.sh all for the suite.
steps: Reproduce: copy an image from the Strata shelf, paste into KGX/GNOME Console — fails with 'No compatible transfer format found'; the same paste into Gmail/Warp (image/png consumers) succeeds. Root cause is the single-mime Meta.SelectionSourceMemory write in shelf.js _writeClipboard.

Intended UI-only approach (calling an existing daemon API, not editing Rust): route binary/image paste-back through proxy.SetClipboard(id) (multi-format via wl-clipboard-rs copy_multi) instead of single-mime Meta.SelectionSourceMemory.

FIRST, verify SetClipboard actually works on the nested GNOME 50 / Mutter: seed a REAL image via StrataCorpus (test-harness/corpus/loader.js seedViaSubmit), call SetClipboard(id) for the stored image, then read the CLIPBOARD selection back the way a paste does and assert the image bytes are retrievable — RED on the current single-mime write, GREEN after the fix.

RESULT (empirical, this stack): SetClipboard fails with the data-control protocol error and writes nothing; there is no UI-only multi-mime selection owner available on Mutter. The fix crosses ADR-0003 (daemon change), so this slice stays passes:false and ships no impl. No case 019) is added to verify.sh because a permanently-failing case would break `verify.sh all` (slice 015) for every other slice.

features.title: Peek image instant + full-res (in-process decode, no glycin/temp-file); Escape dismiss immediate
features.description: Live (post-030, user-confirmed): peeking an image shows a BLACK screen with 'Loading...' for ~2s before the image appears, and Escape to dismiss is still ~1s slow. The 030 agent misattributed the ~2s to the daemon D-Bus transfer; that is wrong — a local IPC blob transfer is milliseconds. The real cost is the UI DECODE path: peek.js writes the image bytes to a TEMP FILE and displays them via CSS background-image: url("file://...") (peek.js ~line 247), which on GNOME invokes GLYCIN — a SANDBOXED image loader that spawns a bwrap subprocess per decode (confirmed: bwrap .../glycin-loaders/... processes observed in the live process list). Cold bwrap-sandbox spin-up + temp-file write ~= the 2s. The SAME heavy glycin-backed GL texture is also slow to tear down, which is the residual ~1s Escape (030 made peek.js close() synchronous but the lag is the texture/glycin teardown, not close()). FIX (UI-only, ADR-0003): decode the image bytes IN-PROCESS from the in-memory blob (GdkPixbuf.Pixbuf.new_from_stream over a Gio.MemoryInputStream -> Clutter/Cogl texture or St image content) with NO temp file, NO file:// CSS, NO glycin sandbox; CACHE the decoded texture per id and PRE-FETCH the focused card's full image in the background so Peek is INSTANT and FULL-RES every time; release textures on dismiss/disable so Escape is immediate and memory stays bounded. DIAGNOSE FIRST and prove with numbers; reject 'inherent' unless measurement shows the daemon GetItemContent return itself is slow (if so, that is a separate v2/daemon finding to record, not a reason to keep the glycin path).
steps: DIAGNOSE with timing: instrument (a) GetItemContent return time, (b) the current temp-file + CSS background-image decode, (c) the new in-process decode + texture upload. Record before/after numbers showing where the ~2s actually goes (expectation: (a) is milliseconds, (b)/glycin is the bulk).

Decode the image bytes IN-PROCESS (e.g. GdkPixbuf from a Gio.MemoryInputStream -> Clutter/Cogl texture or St image content). NO temp file, NO file:// background-image, NO glycin sandbox in the Peek path.

Peek on an image is effectively INSTANT (well under ~150ms once the bytes are in hand) and renders at FULL resolution and FULL brightness (verify the loaded image is bright live, not just the loading state).

Cache the decoded texture per id and pre-fetch the focused card's full-res image in the background so the common peek (the focused card) is instant; release textures on dismiss/disable to bound memory.
Escape (and Space) dismiss the Peek IMMEDIATELY (no perceptible lag) by releasing the in-process texture cheaply — no glycin/sandbox teardown.

TEST: assert the Peek image path uses NO temp file and NO file:// url (the image actor is backed by in-process texture/content, not a CSS background-image url); assert a decoded image content/texture is present after a gated fetch; assert Escape unmaps synchronously; keep 030's brightness + z-order asserts GREEN; teeth-proven. Note clearly which parts are headless-assertable (no-temp-file, content-backed, synchronous unmap, no glycin) vs only live-verifiable (wall-clock instant-ness).
